title: Behavioral and Psychological Drivers of Sustainable Saving and Financial Resilience among Community Households
authors: Erno, G. Y. L.; Grefalde, J. Q.
tldr: Community households in Surigao del Sur show strong debt management but weak budgeting, saving, and investment practices, resulting in low financial resilience.
problem_and_motivation: Sustainable saving behavior and financial capability are critical for household resilience, yet resource-constrained community settings face unique behavioral and psychological barriers.
approach: Quantitative descriptive design with 300 household financial decision-makers across barangays in Tago, Surigao del Sur, Philippines.
Structured survey measuring financial capability domains (budgeting, saving, debt, investment) and resilience indicators.
Anchored in social cognitive theory and behavioral economics.
Analyzes risk perception, decision fatigue, self-control, and emotional management.
findings: Overall financial capability mean of 2.76 indicates partial capability development with significant asymmetry.
Budgeting domain mean of 2.35 indicates weak systematic financial planning.
Saving domain mean of 2.44 reveals limited institutionalized saving behavior.
Strong debt management with prudent borrowing and repayment discipline.
Overall financial resilience level was low.
key_figures_tables: Table 1: Financial capability across four domains → Asymmetric with debt strength, budgeting weakness.
Table 2: Financial resilience level → Low overall resilience reflecting capability gaps.

topic_relevance.contribution_to_field: Provides empirical evidence of asymmetric financial capability in Philippine community households. Shows financial resilience requires balanced integration across all capability domains, not just isolated strengths.
directly_justifies: Households demonstrate strong debt discipline but weak forward-looking planning.
Financial resilience requires balanced integration across all domains.
limits: Single municipality study limits geographic generalizability.
topic_relevance.topic_mapping_rationale: Systematic scan across all 14 domains. Flagged 2.A, 7.A, 13.A (high), 1.C (medium). Rejected algorithmic topics.

limitations: Single municipality (Tago, Surigao del Sur) limits generalizability.
Cross-sectional design captures point-in-time behaviors only.
Self-reported data may introduce response bias.
remember_this: Strong debt discipline masks weak budgeting and saving practices.
Overall financial capability is moderate (2.76/5) with significant asymmetry.
Financial resilience requires balanced capability across all domains.
